description: The tiniest OpenID Certified™ authorization and authentication server you have ever seen.

sources.entry: Tinyauth | Simple authentication middleware for your reverse proxy

summary.one_liner: Tinyauth is a small authentication and authorization server, written in Go, that sits in front of your apps as middleware for reverse proxies or runs standalone, with OAuth/OIDC, LDAP and access-control support.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Tinyauth as an authentication and authorization server that works both as middleware for your apps and as a standalone auth server. It says it supports OAuth, LDAP and access controls. It names Traefik, Nginx and Caddy as supported proxies. The README states that Tinyauth v5.1.0 is OpenID Certified for Basic OP. A docker-compose file with Traefik, Whoami and Tinyauth is mentioned as a demonstration setup. Documentation is hosted on a separate website, and a demo instance is available with default credentials user/password. The README does not list specific 2FA or TOTP features beyond the repository topics.
use_cases: protect self-hosted apps behind a reverse proxy
add single sign-on to homelab services
add OIDC login to apps through Traefik, Nginx or Caddy
authenticate users against an LDAP directory
control which users can access which apps
how_to_run: Follow the getting-started guide in the Tinyauth documentation website
Optionally use the docker-compose file in the development branch, which runs Traefik, Whoami and Tinyauth together
See the contributing guide to run a development server
notable: OpenID Certified for Basic OP (v5.1.0, per README)
Works as proxy middleware or as a standalone auth server
Covers OAuth, LDAP and access-control rules
caveats: README warns the project is in active development and configuration may change often; read release notes before updating
This is the main development branch; the README points to the latest stable tag for production use
Docker-compose example lives in the development branch and may include unreleased changes
